I'm actually very curious how they are effectively splitting training across GPUs. 
I've only ever done training on 1 GPU and never even thought about how grad desc works like that

Multi-GPU training still passes substantial data among the GPUs, so there needs to be network locality (low latency/high bandwidth).   You're basically sharding either the dataset, the model by layers or a combo, then syncing the pieces needing to be redistributed in each epoch.   Strikes me as (still) pretty clunky.   Not to say future models won't allow more loosely-coupled computing clusters... hoping.   I like this article:  https://neptune.ai/blog/multi-gpu-model-training-monitoring-and-optimizing
